key_facts: Grad F presented a sheet containing revised semantic specifications and construction formalisms.
The sheet includes two sides, with one side focusing on semantic specifications and the other on construction formalisms.
There is a distinction between form and meaning types in the construction formalism.
The term 'semantic constraints' was discussed as an alternative to 'constraints', with some reservations due to potential ambiguity.
The concept of 'designates' was introduced as a way to identify the semantic head of a phrase.
The discussion included the idea of having a notation for information structure, including focus and topic.
The group agreed that the current formalism should be used as a basis for further development.
The group decided to focus on defining a set of constructions for the tourist domain and child language learning before tackling more general issues.
Grad A mentioned the possibility of using probabilistic relational models (PRMs) in conjunction with Bayes-nets for construal tasks.
Grad A proposed sending a draft thesis proposal to the group for feedback before leaving.
The group planned to meet again on Thursday at 1 PM or 4 PM, with the final decision left to Grad A.
